contradicting.label: T4E.18's published non-dateline range is false
contradicting.summary: That correction states the nearest feature away from the dateline is '16.6 to 99.3 km', a factor of two to three and not an order of magnitude. The median is right; the range is not. SETH at longitude 155.9 sits 315.1 km out and HOLA at 175.8 sits 247.7, neither near a boundary and both an order of magnitude above the 22.1 km radius median. GRETEL yields no feature at all. RUBY, at longitude 179.0 inside the band named as refused by the off-frame rule, is fine at 67.6 km, so dateline longitude is not sufficient for the failure. The claim stood because the record held one number per storm and the aggregate was taken over a subset nobody named.

contradicting.label: condition 2 on the raw path, measured for the first time
contradicting.summary: Three or more features inside the catalogue radius: 0 of 18 on the raw pass against the SWT pass's 1 of 18, needing 9. It qualifies 'markedly better': the raw pass wins on nearest distance and loses on the count inside the radius.

Although the binomial probability of achieving 3 or fewer successes out of 18 under a null target of 50% (9 of 18) is small (p = 0.0037), confirming the failure to meet the bar, the overall statistical quality of this pipeline is too weak to support any robust positive inferences.

request.instruction: Turn 3. Speak in the seat of confounder_challenge over the evidence shown.
request.system: Attack the causal reading: shared drivers, selection, look-ahead, and any alternative that would produce the same numbers. Name the alternatives you cannot exclude. You are commenting beside the evidence, never on it. Nothing you write can change a claim level, and no claim level will be changed because you asked for one. alternatives: Selection bias in the chosen subset of 18 storms, where geographic and physical characteristics systematically differ from the broader population.
Spatial look-ahead or data leakage in the SWT preprocessing pipeline that utilizes downstream path information not available to the raw pass.
Shared drivers, such as storm intensity or size, which simultaneously determine the catalogue radius (including impossible 0.00 values) and the extraction algorithm's likelihood of success.
structured.argument: The causal attribution of the performance deficit to threshold extraction mechanics is heavily confounded. First, spatial look-ahead in the SWT pipeline may artificially inflate its performance relative to the raw pass, meaning the delta is driven by information leakage rather than extraction robustness. Second, physical characteristics of the storms act as shared drivers: weaker or smaller systems naturally lead to smaller catalogue radii (including invalid 0.00 values) and simultaneously make features harder to extract. Finally, selection effects from arbitrary dateline exclusions prevent establishing a clean causal relationship. Without isolating these confounding factors, the observed numerical differences cannot be causally attributed to the extraction thresholds themselves.

Setting a zero-radius target guarantees physical and mathematical failure regardless of algorithm quality. Second, the spatial scales involved are physically incompatible. A median extraction radius of 22.1 km is characteristic of individual convective cells, whereas the actual feature locations for storms like SETH (315.1 km away) and HOLA (247.7 km away) are on the synoptic scale. At distances exceeding 200 km, any extracted features cannot physically represent the core of the cataloged storm center and are likely unrelated ambient convective systems. Applying a tight median radius to features that naturally span hundreds of kilometers represents a failure to align the extraction mechanics with the physical dimensions of meteorological phenomena.
